title: Boundary semicontinuity of weights on a curve
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a curve over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ in the sense of
[d-real-setup] (smooth, separated, geometrically connected; it need
not be affine, e.g. it may be proper), let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a dense open
immersion with finite complement $S_0$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse Weil sheaf (in the conventions of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]) of rank $r\ge1$ on $U_0$. Assume that for every
closed point $x\in|U_0|$ and every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of the local
Frobenius $F_x$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$ the inequality

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_x^{\beta}
$$

holds for a real number $\beta$ (that is, it has punctual eigenvalue weights at most $\beta$ in the convention of [sk-d-real-weights]). Then the same
inequality holds at every boundary point: for every $s\in S_0$ and
every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_s$ on the middle-extension stalk
$(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar s}$ of
[def-wf-middle-extension],

$$
|\iota(\alpha)|^2\le q_s^{\beta}.
$$

Since $j_*\mathcal F$ restricts to $\mathcal F$ on $U_0$, this says
that $j_*\mathcal F$ has punctual weights at most $\beta$ on all of
$X_0$.

proof.text: Localize at a boundary point. If $S_0$ is empty the assertion is the hypothesis. Otherwise fix $s\in S_0$ and choose an affine open neighborhood $X'_0$ of $s$. The geometric curve $X$ is smooth, nonempty and connected, so [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], clause 1, makes it integral. Thus its nonempty opens, including the base changes of $X'_0$ and $U'_0=U_0\cap X'_0$, are irreducible and connected. The restrictions are still smooth separated finite-type curves, so $X'_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve. In the section formula of [def-wf-middle-extension], for every etale $V\to X'_0$ both $(j_*\mathcal F)|_{X'_0}(V)$ and $j'_*(\mathcal F|_{U'_0})(V)$ equal $\mathcal F(V\times_{X_0}U_0)$. These equalities respect restrictions and Weil maps. They identify the stalks and their Frobenius at $s$. Restriction preserves the hypothesis and rank. It therefore suffices to work on $X'_0$; rename it $X_0$ and rename $U'_0$ as $U_0$.

source.place: Step 0: affine restriction, with the sectionwise comparison written out

proof.text: Let $e_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, $q_x=q^{e_x}$, and list the local eigenvalues with multiplicity as $\alpha_{x,1},\ldots,\alpha_{x,r}$. Put $a_{x,i}=\iota(\alpha_{x,i})$ and $H(T)=L_\iota(U_0,\mathcal F,T)^{-1}=\prod_{x,i}(1-a_{x,i}T^{e_x})$ in [d-real-cohom]. Local finiteness holds because there are finitely many closed points of bounded degree, as stated there. By [lem-wf-point-count-linear-growth] on the affine curve $X_0$, fix $A\geq1$ with $\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^e})\leq Aq^e$ for all $e\geq1$. If $c_e(U_0)$ counts degree-$e$ closed points of $U_0$, the formula of [prop-euler-product] on $X_0$ gives $e c_e(U_0)\leq e c_e(X_0)\leq\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^e})$. Hence $c_e(U_0)\leq Aq^e$. Notice that the counting theorem is applied to the affine ambient curve; no affineness claim about $U_0$ is needed.

source.place: Step 1, point-count estimate; unit proof first paragraph

proof.text:
Put $R=q^{-\beta/2-1}>0$. Fix a real $0\leq t<R$ and index $I$ by the pairs $(x,i)$ above. The hypothesis gives $|a_{x,i}|\leq q^{e_x\beta/2}$, and therefore
$$\sum_{(x,i)\in I}|a_{x,i}|t^{e_x}\leq rA\sum_{e\geq1}(q^{1+\beta/2}t)^e<\infty.$$
Set $u_{x,i}=|a_{x,i}|t^{e_x}\geq0$. By [lem-wf-summable-finite-subset-products], $\sum_{S\subset I\text{ finite}}\prod_{j\in S}u_j$ is finite. If $H(T)=\sum_n h_nT^n$, expand its coefficient as the finite sum over subsets $S$ with $\sum_{(x,i)\in S}e_x=n$. Its absolute value is at most the sum of $\prod_{(x,i)\in S}|a_{x,i}|$ over those subsets. Consequently every finite partial sum of $\sum_n|h_n|t^n$ is bounded by the displayed finite-subset sum. The nonnegative partial sums increase and are bounded, so they converge. This proves $R(H)\geq R$ in [d-real-series].

source.place: Step 1, convergence input; unit proof first paragraph, inverse-Euler-series coefficient estimate

proof.text:
Write $J=j_*\mathcal F$ and $V=\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$. The endpoint identification of [lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints] gives, Frobenius-equivariantly,
$$H_c^2(X,J)\simeq Q(-1),\qquad Q=V_{\pi_1(U)}.$$
Its hypotheses hold: the ambient $X_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve by step 1, $j$ is dense open, and $\mathcal F$ is lisse Weil. We use only this identification, not the node's additional assertion for a pure sheaf. It is the existing interface for the unit's localization and top-degree duality argument; in particular it already accounts for the finite boundary correction.

Choose a closed point $x$ of $U_0$: this curve is nonempty and finite type over the Noetherian field $k_0$, hence Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is Kolmogorov by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]: two points with the same closure would be two generic points of that irreducible closed subset and hence equal. Thus [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] applies. By [lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], choose a degree-one element $\gamma$ of $W(U_0)$. On $Q$ the geometric subgroup acts trivially. By [p-real-operations], $F_x$ has degree $e_x\geq1$, so $F_x\gamma^{-e_x}$ acts trivially on $Q$ and its action there is $\gamma^{e_x}$. If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $\gamma$ on $Q$, an eigenvector shows that $\lambda^{e_x}$ is an eigenvalue of $F_x$ on $Q$. By [p-linear-filtration] it occurs also on $V$, and [p-real-operations] identifies this spectrum with that on $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$. Thus $|\iota(\lambda)|^{2e_x}\leq q^{e_x\beta}$, whence $|\iota(\lambda)|\leq q^{\beta/2}$. This uses only a geometrically constant quotient, not an arbitrary Frobenius lift on $V$.

Apply [lem-wf-tate-twist-frobenius] with $m=-1$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$: its geometric Frobenius is multiplication by $q$. Together with step 4, this says that the eigenvalues $\mu_j$ of $F$ on $H_c^2(X,J)$ are $q\lambda_j$, where $\lambda_j$ are the eigenvalues considered in step 5. Hence $|\iota(\mu_j)|\leq q^{\beta/2+1}=R^{-1}$. Put
$$D(T)=\det(1-TF\mid H_c^2(X,J)),\qquad N(T)=\det(1-TF\mid H_c^1(X,J)),$$
with coefficients mapped to $\mathbf C$ by $\iota$. Thus $D(T)=\prod_j(1-\iota(\mu_j)T)$ and every factor is nonzero for $|T|<R$. If $H_c^2=0$, the product is empty and $D=1$.

source.place: Step 2, Tate twist and denominator bound

proof.text:
For each boundary point put $P_s(T)=\iota\det(1-F_sT\mid J_{\bar s})$ and set $B(T)=\prod_{s\in S_0}P_s(T^{e_s})$, a finite polynomial product with $B(0)=1$. By the definition of the locally finite Euler product [d-real-cohom], separating the closed points into $U_0$ and $S_0$ gives $L_\iota(X_0,J,T)=L_\iota(U_0,\mathcal F,T)B(T)^{-1}$. The exact identity in [lem-wf-euler-product-middle-extension] gives $L_\iota(X_0,J,T)=N(T)/D(T)$. All these are identities of formal series with unit constant term. Multiplying them yields
$$B(T)^{-1}=N(T)D(T)^{-1}H(T).$$

source.place: Step 3, formal Euler-product identity; unit proof second paragraph

proof.text:
For $0\leq t<R$, expand each denominator factor as $(1-\iota(\mu_j)T)^{-1}=\sum_{n\geq0}\iota(\mu_j)^nT^n$. Its absolute coefficient sum at $t$ is the finite geometric sum $1/(1-|\iota(\mu_j)|t)$. The product has only finitely many such factors. For two series $a,b$ with finite absolute coefficient sums at $t$, the triangle inequality gives
$$\sum_n\left|\sum_{i+j=n}a_i b_j\right|t^n\leq\left(\sum_i|a_i|t^i\right)\left(\sum_j|b_j|t^j\right)<\infty.$$
Use this finite number of times for $D^{-1}$, the polynomial $N$ and the series $H$ of step 3. Step 7 then gives $R(B^{-1})\geq R$ in [d-real-series]. This is the finite geometric-series and coefficient-convolution calculation, requiring no theorem about cancellation of poles of unrelated factors.

source.place: Steps 2–3, convergence of the rational product; unit proof second paragraph

proof.text:
Apply [lem-wf-rational-series-pole-radius] with its $P=1$, $Q=B$ and $f=B^{-1}$. If $B(z)=0$, it gives $R\leq R(B^{-1})\leq|z|$; thus $B$ has no zero in $|z|<R$. Let $\alpha$ be an eigenvalue of $F_s$ on $J_{\bar s}$. Frobenius is invertible, so $a=|\iota(\alpha)|>0$. Choose $z\in\mathbf C$ with $z^{e_s}=\iota(\alpha)^{-1}$ (take an $e_s$th root using polar coordinates). The eigenvector equation makes $P_s(z^{e_s})=0$, so $B(z)=0$ and $a^{-1/e_s}=|z|\geq R$. Since $e_s\geq1$ this is precisely
$$|\iota(\alpha)|^2\leq q^{e_s(\beta+2)}=q_s^{\beta+2}.$$
The use of $P=1$ rules out cancellation without any positivity assumption on the boundary factors.

For $n\geq1$, form $\mathcal F^{\otimes n}$. By the tensor equivalence [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] it is a lisse Weil sheaf of rank $r^n\geq1$. By [p-real-operations] and [p-linear-spectra], its local eigenvalues are products of $n$ original eigenvalues. Their squared $\iota$-moduli are at most $q_x^{n\beta}$. Hence steps 1–9 apply to it, with $n\beta$ replacing $\beta$.

source.place: Step 4, tensor powers preserve the punctual upper bound

proof.text:
By the Frobenius-equivariant identification [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants], choose a nonzero eigenvector $v\in V^{I_s}$ with eigenvalue $\alpha$. For every $n\geq1$, $v^{\otimes n}$ is fixed by $I_s$ and a residue Frobenius sends it to $\alpha^n v^{\otimes n}$. This tensor is nonzero: choose a coordinate functional $f$ with $f(v)=1$ and apply $f^{\otimes n}$. Apply the same cited stalk identification to $\mathcal F^{\otimes n}$. It shows that $\alpha^n$ is a boundary eigenvalue for that sheaf. Therefore the preliminary bound gives
$$|\iota(\alpha)|^{2n}\leq q_s^{n\beta+2}\quad(n\geq1).$$
No equality between tensor products of invariants and invariants of tensor products is assumed.

source.place: Step 4, invariant tensor eigenvector and its nonvanishing

proof.text: Put $a=|\iota(\alpha)|>0$. Taking logarithms of step 11 and dividing by $n$ gives $2\log a\leq\beta\log q_s+2\log q_s/n$ for every positive integer $n$. If $\delta=2\log a-\beta\log q_s>0$, choose $n>2\log q_s/\delta$, contradicting that inequality. Thus $2\log a\leq\beta\log q_s$, so $a^2\leq q_s^\beta$. This proves the boundary assertion for every $s$, and step 1 returns it to the original curve. On $U_0$, the section formula in [def-wf-middle-extension] restricts to $\mathcal F$ itself, so the hypothesis gives the same bound there. In the convention [sk-d-real-weights], the whole middle extension has punctual eigenvalue weights at most $\beta$.

source.place: Step 4, limit and conclusion on all closed points

proof_origin.place: Steps 0–4, read with sk-p-real-semi.proof.md: inverse-Euler-series majorant and formal boundary-polynomial argument; full calculations supplied in the split.

Supplies Noetherian and hence quasi-compact hypotheses for selecting a closed point in the quotient-spectrum argument.
Uniqueness of a generic point implies the Kolmogorov hypothesis needed to select a closed point.
Existence of a closed point in the nonempty quasi-compact scheme U_0 is a topological tool for the quotient-spectrum argument.
The quotient by geometric monodromy factors through the degree map, as used explicitly in unit paragraph 2.
Identifies local Frobenius with its representation operator and gives its degree, for the quotient and tensor calculations in unit paragraphs 2 and 3.
The (-1) twist multiplies geometric Frobenius by q on Spec k_0, needed in the unit top-degree bound.
General formal polynomial-identity radius obstruction, applied with numerator 1 to the boundary polynomial; it supplies the unit pole argument without a positivity hypothesis.
Exact tensor equivalence supplies lisse Weil tensor powers for unit paragraph 3, without changing its route.
